scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all reach across the
data-center fabric -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is unreachable, though pc_0_0
can still ping its own gateway 10.0.0.1. The NOC adds that both
spine routers reported their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_0 going
down at the same moment, while the leaf's uplink interfaces still
show UP. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on leaf_router_0_0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 is the top-of-rack leaf for pc_0_0
  (host subnet 10.0.0.0/24 on eth2). Its only fabric attachment is
  EBGP: neighbor 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0, AS 65100) on eth0 and
  neighbor 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1, AS 65101) on eth1. With bgpd
  dead the leaf stops learning 10.0.1.0/24 and stops advertising
  10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_0 is isolated from the fabric even though every
  physical link is still UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- this lab
  keeps its config in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so a restart fully restores
  the BGP configuration and sessions.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03 on this fabric): bgpd is killed
together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh
remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is
missing/empty on leaf_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on leaf_router_0_0. Unlike the vtysh-configured
kath labs, this lab has a persistent /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart
brings bgpd back WITH its full BGP configuration; the sessions to both
spines re-establish and pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 again.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The FRR routing stack on `leaf_router_0_0` — specifically the `bgpd` daemon and the overarching `frr.service` unit, both of which are `inactive (dead)`.

**Mechanism:** In this DC Clos BGP fabric, each leaf router establishes eBGP sessions to both spine routers and advertises its directly-attached host prefix (10.0.0.0/24 in this case). When `frr.service` died on `leaf_router_0_0`, `bgpd` terminated, tearing down both eBGP sessions simultaneously (explaining why both `spine_router_0_0` and `spine_router_0_1` saw the session go `Active` at the same moment). Without `bgpd`, `leaf_router_0_0` no longer advertises 10.0.0.0/24 to the spines, and no longer receives routes for 10.0.1.0/24 from the spines. Its kernel routing table is left with only three directly-connected prefixes and no inter-fabric routes. When `pc_0_0` sends traffic toward `pc_0_1` (10.0.1.2), its gateway `leaf_router_0_0` has no forwarding entry for 10.0.1.0/24 and returns an ICMP `Destination Net Unreachable` — matching the observed symptom exactly.

**Localization:** `leaf_router_0_0`, `frr.service` / `bgpd` process. `watchfrr` is also absent, so no automated daemon-restart guard is active. The uplink interfaces (eth0, eth1) remain physically UP with their /31 point-to-point addresses, consistent with the NOC observation.

**Root cause:** The FRR service (`frr.service`) is dead on `leaf_router_0_0`, causing `bgpd` to be absent, collapsing both spine eBGP sessions and removing all BGP-learned routes.

**Fix:** Restart FRR on `leaf_router_0_0` — `systemctl start frr` — which will bring up `watchfrr`, `zebra`, and `bgpd`, re-establish eBGP sessions to both spines, and restore full fabric reachability.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies leaf_router_0_0 as the affected device multiple times.
Agent explicitly identifies bgpd as inactive/dead on leaf_router_0_0 (BGP daemon down).

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0
per_axis.rationale: The report localizes the failure to leaf_router_0_0 but does not explicitly state that the spines, super-spine, and leaf_router_0_1 (and their other sessions) remained healthy/Established, so it fails to explicitly exonerate the rest of the fabric.
Proposes restarting/starting the FRR service on leaf_router_0_0, which will restore bgpd and re-establish the eBGP sessions as required.

The investigation log shows concrete evidence (pc pings returning 'Destination Net Unreachable', bgp_snapshot flagging bgpd/watchfrr missing, and leaf_router_0_0 systemctl status=inactive with no bgpd process and no learned routes), and the writeup's chain (FRR dead → bgpd absent → BGP sessions down → no learned routes → unreachable host) follows directly from those observations.
